payload.summary: Implemented workflow module frontend routes, workflow pages, notification bell, socket invalidation provider, API endpoint wiring, and route/sidebar integration; frontend npm run build passed.
Workflow and notification feature files were copied directly into C:/test-project; temp worktree is staging-only and not source of truth.
Fixed workflow API contract mismatches: permissions field names, list query params, PUT update method, resubmit payload shape, and disabled mock mode to use backend API.

Completed missing Agent 3 frontend wiring: create/edit workflow pages now save steps with replaceSteps, edit page uses definition builder UI, action permissions/revision/stale handling aligned, frontend specs updated, build passed.
cd frontend; npm run build passed with existing Vite large chunk warning.
Added WORK-030 frontend specs and tightened workflow step builder min/max/save guards.
Final cd frontend; npm run build passed after step builder guard changes.
Added shared useClickOutside hook and wired NotificationBell to close when pointerdown occurs outside its container.
Created draft work item WORK-032 for auth refresh token backend API and frontend Axios silent-refresh wiring.
Internal app route changes must use React Router client-side navigation such as useNavigate; full-page window.location reloads are forbidden for internal routes.

Rebuilt workflows/create Form Schema and Approval Steps as table-style multi-row editors with checkbox selection, ContextMenu actions, Zod/RHF field arrays, grid navigation, field-error mapping, and replaceSteps persistence.
cd frontend; npm run build passed after WorkflowCreatePage table editor changes.

Aligned WorkflowListPage with frontend rules: list query state now drives API params/query keys, status filter added, updatedAt sortable column added, fixed scroll height and sticky header added, spec updated.
cd frontend; npm run build passed after WorkflowListPage rule-alignment changes.
User asked to fix notifications so the frontend reads them from the database instead of mocks, and to make realtime actually work

Socket realtime was silently dead: backend emitted workflow.request.* and notification.created per contract 9.2 but the client subscribed to workflow-request:updated / notification:updated. No name matched, so no handler ever fired. No error or warning was produced.
notification.api.ts now calls GET /api/notifications through baseApiService with the mock path removed, and reads unreadCount from response meta rather than counting the current page
useWorkflowSocket.ts subscribes to the eight frozen contract event names declared as constants, splits workflow and notification invalidation, and refreshes both on connect/reconnect
npm run build passed; verified all eight socket event names now match the backend emitter character-for-character and no mock remains in the notification path
notification-workflow.md documents the real API data source, why unreadCount must come from meta, and that socket event names are frozen and fail silently when mismatched

Rebuilt WorkflowEditPage to match WorkflowCreatePage table-editor UI for Form Schema and Approval Steps with RHF field arrays, Zod, checkboxes, ContextMenu, grid navigation, field-error mapping, flow preview, and replaceSteps persistence.
cd frontend; npm run build passed after WorkflowEditPage table editor changes.
Updated workflow-requests/new with MUI-styled searchable react-select workflow picker and 12-column DynamicFormRenderer layout where textarea spans 12 and other fields span 3.
cd frontend; npm run build passed after workflow request submit UI update.
DynamicFormRenderer now uses RequiredHeader for required workflow form fields and sorts textarea fields without mutating props.
cd frontend; npm run build passed after dynamic form required marker update.

User reported POST /api/workflow-requests returning 500 and clarified the changed actor-resolution behaviour is intentional, asking for the spec to be updated to match the code rather than the code changed back

Root cause of the 500: no employee row has user_id set, so the seeded admin account resolves to no Employee and employeeId reaches Prisma as undefined. Data prerequisite, not a code defect under the current intended behaviour.

User decision: resolveActorEmployee does not throw when no Employee is linked. Submit therefore surfaces 500 from Prisma and list endpoints return an empty result instead of 403. Spec updated to describe implemented behaviour rather than reverting the code.

submit-workflow-request.md and list-workflow-requests.md updated: removed the 403 WORKFLOW_ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED path from actor resolution, documented the 500 and empty-list outcomes, and recorded the employees.user_id data prerequisite in Ambiguities
Documented user's choice to keep DynamicFormRenderer fields.sort((a,b)=>...) behavior so textarea fields render after smaller fields.
User hit a failure calling POST /api/auth/invitations/accept; the endpoint did not exist. User asked to implement it.

Root cause was a missing route, not a bug: AuthController had only login/me/logout/change-password/forgot-password and InvitationsController only POST /invitations, so the accept route returned 404. Known WORK-024 gap.

Implemented POST /api/auth/invitations/accept: AcceptInvitationDto, IInvitationsService.acceptInvitation, and a dedicated InvitationAcceptController mounted at auth/invitations so the route stays unauthenticated

Separate controller rather than a method on InvitationsController, because that class applies JwtAuthGuard at class level and this endpoint must be public - the raw token is the only credential and the account does not exist yet

acceptInvitation uses prisma.transaction for the three-table write (create User, set employees.user_id, close invitation) because it spans three delegates and no inherited BaseService method can express it; all other writes in the service still use inherited methods

tsc --noEmit clean outside pre-existing spec-file failures; npm run build passed; verified the user-supplied token resolves to a SENT non-expired invitation whose employee has userId null, so it is redeemable

accept-invitation.md records the implemented controller placement and rationale plus password-policy, generic-not-found and transaction notes; added test/http/invitations/invitations.http with happy path and five negative cases
User reviewed InvitationAcceptPage and asked why it calls the API on mount and where the password is entered, since the API requires one

InvitationAcceptPage was written before the backend endpoint existed and guessed the contract wrong: a useEffect posted token alone on mount, there was no password input, and AcceptInvitationPayload had no password fields. It could never have succeeded and would burn the token on page open.

Rewrote InvitationAcceptPage as a react-hook-form + zod form with password and confirmPassword inputs; the mutation now runs only on submit, maps field errors onto inputs, shows token failures as a page-level message, and navigates to /login on success

AcceptInvitationPayload gained password and confirmPassword so TypeScript enforces the real contract; acceptInvitationSchema added to auth.schemas.ts reusing newPasswordSchema so the client policy cannot drift from the backend
npm run build passed after the rewrite
invitation-accept.md now lists the real implemented file paths and states explicitly that the accept API must fire only on submit, recording the on-mount bug that was fixed

Aligned MyRequestsPage and ReviewerInboxPage with frontend list rules: debounced search, status filter, submittedAt sort column, fixed-height scroll, sticky header, full pagination meta, and mock list filtering.
cd frontend; npm run build passed after workflow request list alignment.
